title: Except — Set Difference
description: Learn to find elements in one collection that don't exist in another using Except.

data.text: The `Except` method requires two collections. It returns a new collection with elements from the first collection that do **not** exist in the second collection.

data.title: Except with Primitive Types
data.content: Finding elements in first collection not in second

data.text: For complex types, you need to implement `IEqualityComparer<T>` to get correct results:

data.title: Except with Custom Comparer
data.content: Finding students in first list not in second

data.title: Not Supported in Query Syntax
data.text: The Except operator is not supported in C# or VB.NET query syntax. Use method syntax only.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Except returns elements from first collection not in second
data.takeaway: Continue to the next lesson to learn about the Intersect operator.
